questions.question: Which of the following is **NOT **a use of washing soda?

options.text: It can be used as a cleaning agent for domestic purposes.
It is used in glass, soap and paper industries
It is used for removing permanent hardness of water.
It is used to make drinking water free from germs.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is used to make drinking water free from germs**__.

__
 
• **Washing soda** is a chemical compound with the formula **Na₂CO₃**, known as **sodium carbonate**. It is a salt of carbonic acid. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

__
 
• **Properties of a Washing soda-**

 
 
• It is a transparent crystalline solid.
 
• It is one of the few metal carbonates which are soluble in water.
 
• It is alkaline with a pH level of 11, it turns red litmus to blue.
 
• It has detergent properties or cleansing properties because it can remove dirt and grease from dirty clothes, etc.
 
• It attacks dirt and grease to form water-soluble products, which are then washed away on rinsing with water.
 
• It is used in glass, soap and paper industries.
 
• It is also used in the manufacture of sodium compounds such as borax.
 
• It is used for removing the permanent hardness of the water.
 
 
 
• **Bleaching powder is used to make drinking water free from germs**__.

questions.question:
Which of the given Articles of the Constitution of India mentions the following?

"There shall be a council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President who shall in the exercise of his functions, act in accordance with such advice."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 74(1)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 74(1)**__

 __
 
• There shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President who shall, in the exercise of his functions, act in accordance with such advice: Provided that the President may require the Council of Ministers to reconsider such advice, either generally or otherwise, and the President shall act in accordance with the advice tendered after such reconsideration.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 74(2)**

 
 
• The question of whether any and if so what, advice was tendered by Ministers to the President shall not be inquired into in any court.
 
 
 
• **Article 71(1)**
 
 
• All doubts and disputes arising out of or in connection with the election of a president or vice President shall be inquired into and decided by the Supreme court whose decision shall be final.
 
 
 
• **Article 71(2)**
 
 
• If the election of a person as President or Vice President is declared void by the Supreme court, acts done by him in the exercise and performance of the powers and duties of the office of President or Vice President, as the case may be, on or before the date of the decision of the Supreme Court shall not be invalidated by reason of that declaration.

questions.question: Bhaskaravarman of the Varman dynasty ruled in the _____ region.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kamarupa**__.

__
 
• **Bhaskaravarman of the Varman dynasty ruled in the Kamarupa region**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• **The Varman dynasty** was part of the Kamarupa kingdom of Assam.

 
 
• Its reign was from 350 CE to 655 CE and Pushyavarman was its founder.
 
 
 
• After being captured by the Gaur king during his father's reign, Bhaskaravarman was able to re-establish Varman's rule. 
 
 
• **He made political alliances with Harshavardhana of Thaneswar, against the alliance of the Gauda and East Malwa.**
 
• He was visited by Xuanzang and Li Yi-Piao, the envoy of the Tang dynasty who has left accounts of the king and the kingdom.​
 
• He was the first Kamarupa king to claim descent from the mythical Narakasura, Bhagadatta, and Vajradatta.
 
• After his death, Salasthambha, who established the Mlechchha dynasty, acquired power in the Kamarupa Kingdom.
 
• He issued the Dubi and Nidhanpur copper plate grants, re-issued after his ancestor Bhutivarman, and a clay seal found in Nalanda.

questions.question: Which of the following types of rocks are formed by the lithification process?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sedimentary rocks**__.

__
 
• **Sedimentary rocks are formed by the lithification process**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Lithification:**

 
 
• It refers to the process that loose and under-consolidated sediment particles transform into hard and solid rocks.
 
• This process includes a number of geological processes, such as consolidation, deep bury, cementation, recrystallization and dehydration.
 
 
 
• **Igneous Rocks**
 
 
• As igneous rocks form out of magma and lava from the interior of the earth, they are known as primary rocks.
 
• The igneous rocks (Ignis – in Latin means ‘Fire’) are formed when magma cools and solidifies.
 
• When magma in its upward movement cools and turns into a solid form it is called igneous rock.
 
• The process of cooling and solidification can happen in the earth’s crust or on the surface of the earth.
 
• Igneous rocks are classified based on texture which depends upon the size and arrangement of grains or other physical conditions of the materials.
 
• **Granite, gabbro, pegmatite, basalt, volcanic breccia, **and tuff are some of the examples of igneous rocks.
 
 
 
• **Sedimentary Rocks**
 
 
• The word ‘sedimentary’ is derived from the Latin word sedimentum, which means settling.
 
• Rocks (igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic) of the earth’s surface are exposed to denudational agents and are broken up into various sizes of fragments.
 
• Such fragments are transported by different exogenous agencies and deposited.
 
• These deposits through compaction turn into rocks.
 
• In many sedimentary rocks, the layers of deposits retain their characteristics even after lithification.
 
• Hence, we see a number of layers of varying thickness in sedimentary rocks like** sandstone, shale, geyserite, chalk, limestone, coal etc.**
 
 
 
• **Metamorphic Rocks**
 
 
• Metamorphic means ‘change of form’.
 
• These rocks form under the action of pressure, volume, and temperature (PVT) change.
 
• Metamorphism occurs when rocks are forced down to lower levels by tectonic processes or when molten magma rising through the crust comes in contact with the crustal rocks or the underlying rocks are subjected to great amounts of pressure by overlying rocks.
 
• Metamorphic rocks are formed due to the proximity of sedimentary rocks with molten magma.
 
• Mechanical disruption and reorganization of the original minerals within rocks due to breaking and crushing without any appreciable chemical changes are called dynamic metamorphism.
 
• **Examples- Marble, Quartzite, Schist, etc.**

questions.question: What is the generic name of calcium sulphate hemihydrate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plaster of Paris**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Plaster of Paris is the generic name of calcium sulphate hemihydrate-CaSO₄. 1/2H₂O**__.

 __
 
• Plaster of Paris is manufactured by heating gypsum at 423K or 150o C/300o F.
 
• On heating gypsum at 423 K, it loses water molecules and becomes calcium sulfate hemihydrate. This product is known as the plaster of Paris.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Application of Plaster of Paris**-

 
 
• It is used as a building material as a protective coating on walls and ceilings.
 
• It is used as a moulding and vesting agent for decorative elements.
 
• It is also used for aesthetic touch to the construction elements.
 
• It is also field as plaster in orthopedics and as a filling material by dentists, etc.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Baking soda is also known as sodium bicarbonate** or bicarbonate of soda.
 
• **Vinegar is also known as acetic acid**. It typically contains 5–8% acetic acid by volume.

questions.question: Which of the following keyboard shortcuts will you press in order to minimise all programs on a computer screen and display the desktop?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Windows + D**__.

__
 
• **Windows + D- Minimise all programs on a computer screen and display the desktop**__
 
• Windows + M- Minimize all windows
 
• Windows + C- Nothing in particular
 
• Windows + F- Start a Feedback dialog

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **__Confusion Points__**

__
 
• Windows key + M minimizes all open windows – “M” for “Minimize.”
 
 
• Win + M minimizes all opened windows excluding those which do not support WM_MINIMIZE;
 
 
 
• Windows key + D also minimizes all open windows – “D” for “Desktop.”
 
 
• **Win + D shows the desktop in any case.** ​
 
 

​As Question is about minimising all programs on a computer screen and **displaying the desktop.** Hence **Windows key + D** is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Windows logo key + E- Open Computer
 
• Windows logo key + F- Start a Feedback dialog
 
• Ctrl+ Windows logo key + F- Search for computers (if you're on a network)

questions.question: Which of the following is the largest brackish water lake in Asia?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chilika**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chilika is the largest brackish water lake in Asia**__.

 __
 
• It is Asia’s largest and the world’s second-largest lagoon.
 
• It spreads over the Puri, Khurda, and Ganjam districts of Odisha on the east coast of India, at the mouth of the Daya River.
 
• It flows into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• In 1981, it was designated the first Indian wetland of international importance under the Ramsar Convention.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Loktak Lake **is the largest natural freshwater lake in India. It is famous for the phumdis (heterogeneous mass of vegetation, soil and organic matter at various stages of decomposition) floating over it.
 
• **Pulicat Lagoon** is the second largest brackish water lagoon in India. It is along the Coromandel Coast.
 
• **Wular Lake **is sited in Bandipora district in Jammu and Kashmir. The lake basin was formed as a result of tectonic activity and is fed by the Jhelum River.

questions.question: In 2020, the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded jointly to Harvey J Alter, Michael Houghton and Charles M Rice for the discovery of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**hepatitis C virus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In 2020, the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded jointly to Harvey J Alter, Michael Houghton, and Charles M Rice for the discovery of the hepatitis C virus**__.

 __
 
• The methodical studies of transfusion-associated hepatitis by 2020 Medicine Laureate Harvey J. Alter demonstrated that an unknown virus was a common cause of chronic hepatitis.
 
• Michael Houghton – awarded the 2020 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine – used an untested strategy to isolate the genome of the new virus that was named Hepatitis C virus.
 
• Medicine Laureate Charles M. Rice provided the final evidence showing that the Hepatitis C virus alone could cause hepatitis
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hepatitis, from the Greek name for liver and inflammation, is a disease characterized by poor appetite, vomiting, fatigue and jaundice – yellow discoloration of the skin and eyes**.

 
 
• Chronic hepatitis leads to liver damage, which may progress to cirrhosis and liver cancer.
 
• Viral infection is the leading cause of hepatitis, with some forms persisting without symptoms for many years before life-threatening complications develop.

questions.question: In which of the following caves Is the painting named ‘Padmapanl Bodhisattva’ found?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ajanta Cave No. 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The painting named ‘Padmapanl Bodhisattva’ is found in Ajanta Cave No. 1**__.
 
• Out of the 30 excavated caves, five (cave no. 9, 10, 19, 26, and 29) are chaitya grihas (prayer halls) and the rest are viharas (monasteries).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• In date and style, these caves can be divided into two broad phases-
 
 
• ** Phase I (2nd Century to 1st Century BCE)**

 
 
• **The earliest excavations were done by the Satavahanas and belong to the Hinayana (Theravada) phase of Buddhism.**
 
• The object of worship is a stupa here.
 
• Caves 9, 10, 12, 13, and 15A belong to this era.
 
 
 
• Phase II (5th Century AD to 6th Century AD)
 
 
• These excavations are a major contribution of the Vakatakas and Chalukyas.
 
• It belongs to the Mahayana phase of Buddhism which is mostly a Post Gupta age.
 
 
 
 
 
• **In Buddhism, a bodhisattva is any person who is on the path towards Buddhahood. Padmapani in Sanskrit literally translates into one who holds the lotus**.
 
• In the painting, the bodhisattva is holding a blue lotus in his right hand. The eyes are half-closed and look downward

questions.question: Which of the following rivers originates from the state of Rajasthan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Banas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Banas river originates from the state of Rajasthan**__.

 __
 
• The river **originates from the Khamnor hills of the Aravali range near Kumbhalgarh**.
 
• It is also known as 'Van ki Asha' (Hope of forest).
 
• It flows northeast through the Mewar region of Rajasthan and meets the Chambal near the village of Rameshwar in Sawai Madhopur district.
 
• **Berach and Menali are the right bank tributaries of the Banas river. **
 
• **Kothari, Khari, Dai, Dheel River, Sohadara River, Morel, and Kalisil are the left bank tributaries of Banas river.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Chambal River**

 
 
• It is the tributary of the Yamuna River.
 
• It rises in the Vindhyachal range South of Mhow, the western state of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• It flows from the north into the southeastern state of Rajasthan.
 
• It ends on the confluence of five rivers which includes the Chambal, Kwari, Yamuna, Sind, Pahuj, at Pachnada near Bhareh in Uttar Pradesh, at the border of Bhind and Etawah districts.
 
• Major Tributary - Kshipra, Kalisindh, Parvati, Bansa, Newaj, Kwari, Sindh, etc.
 
 
 
• **Narmada River**
 
 
• It originates from the Narmada Kund located in Amarkantak, Anuppur district in Madhya Pradesh.
 
• The major tributaries of the Narmada are Barna, Tawa, Kanar, Kolar, Man, Hatni, Uri, Shakkar, etc.
 
• It flows westwards before falling into the Gulf of Khambhat.
 
• The Narmada river is the longest river in Madhya Pradesh and it's called "The Lifeline of Madhya Pradesh".
 
• The waterfalls created by the Narmada River include Kapil Dhara and Dudh Dhara Falls (Anuppur), Dhuandhar Falls (Bhedaghat, Jabalpur), Sahasradhara Falls (Maheshwar, Khargone), Dardhi Falls, Manadhata Falls, etc.
 
 
 
• **Mahi River**
 
 
• It rises in Madhya Pradesh and, after flowing through the Vagad region of Rajasthan, enters Gujarat and flows into the Arabian Sea.
 
• It is one of Five west-flowing rivers in India, along with Tapti River, Sabarmati River, Luni River (Endorheic river) and the Narmada River.
 
• Tributaries- Som, Anas, and Panam.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• For the Moon or an artificial satellite body moving around the Earth in an elliptical orbit, the distance between the object and the Earth changes throughout the orbit.
 
• The Moon's orbit around Earth is elliptical.
 
• **The point of the orbit closest to Earth is called perigee, while the point farthest from Earth is known as apogee**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• At the point of perigree in the orbit, the object is moving at its maximum speed (Kepler’s Second Law).
 
• An **apsis** is the farthest or nearest point in the orbit of a planetary body about its primary body.
 
 
• The Earth's two apsides are the farthest point- aphelion, and the nearest point- perihelion, of its orbit around the host Sun.
 
 
 
• **The point of maximum separation from the Earth is known as the apogee**. The apogee refers specifically to orbits around the Earth, and is equivalent to the apoapsis of a general orbit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The terms** perihelion **and** aphelion** describe different points in our planet’s orbit of the Sun. This can also apply to other planets, comets, or bodies. 
 
• **Aphelion** is the point of the Earth’s orbit that is farthest away from the Sun. It always happens in early July, about two weeks after the June solstice, 
 
• **Perihelion** is the point of the Earth’s orbit that is nearest to the Sun. This always happens in early January, about two weeks after the December Solstice.
 
• The words come from Ancient Greek, in which** helios means “Sun,” apo means “far,” and peri means “close.”**

questions.question: Who among the following became the youngest speaker of Lok Sabha till March 2021?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ganti Mohana Chandra Balayogi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ganti Mohana Chandra Balayogi became the youngest speaker of Lok Sabha till March 2021**__.

 __
 
• **He had the distinction of having been elected Speaker of the Twelfth Lok Sabha and re-elected unanimously as the Speaker of the Thirteenth Lok Sabha.**
 
• He was handpicked by Telugu Desam Party (TDP) supremo N. Chandrababu Naidu in 1998 to become the youngest and first Dalit Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
 
• As Speaker, Balayogi was the Chairman of the Business Advisory Committee, Rules Committee and General Purposes Committee.
 
• Balayogi was also the Chairman of the Standing Committee of the Conference of Presiding Officers of Legislative Bodies in India.
 
• The Speaker is elected by the Lok Sabha from amongst its members.
 
 
• He is the protector of the members' rights and privileges, the House as a whole, and their committees.
 
• He appoints the chairman of all the parliamentary committees of the Lok Sabha and supervises their functioning.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Meira Kumar was the 15th Speaker** of Lok Sabha from 2009 to 2014.
 
• **Sumitra Mahajan was the 16th Speaker** of Lok Sabha from 2014 to 2019.
 
• **PA Sangma was the 11th Speaker **of Lok Sabha from from 1996 to 1998.

questions.question: Which has been India's most successful sport in the history of Olympic games having won medals maximum number of times till December 2020?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Field Hockey**__.

__
 
• **Field Hockey has been India's most successful sport in the history of Olympic games having won medals maximum number of times till December 2020**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• India's team has won **eight gold medals** in **1928, 1932, 1936, 1948, 1952, 1956, 1964, and 1980.**

 
 
• India also has the best overall performance in Olympic history with 83 victories out of the 134 matches played.
 
• They are also the only team to ever win the Olympics without conceding a single goal in 1928 and 1956.
 
• In 1928, the team won its first Olympic gold medal and until 1960, the Indian men's team remained unbeaten in the Olympics, winning six gold medals in a row.
 
• India also won the World Cup in 1975.

questions.question: Down Syndrome, which causes learning difficulties and physical health development delays and disabilities, is a:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**genetic disease**__.

__
 
• **Down Syndrome is a genetic disease**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Down syndrome** is a genetic condition that arises** due to the presence of an extra chromosome 21.**

 
 
• Here, chromosome 21 is repeated thrice (trisomy 21), instead of showing up twice in a normal individual.
 
• The karyotype of Down syndrome is represented as 47, XX, +21 (females) and 47, XY, +21 (males)
 
• **Some of the most common are characteristics of down syndrome:**
 
 
• Flat face, round head, and typical epicanthic fold of the eyes
 
• Short, broad hands
 
• Mental retardation Hypotonia – poor muscle tone
 
• Short stature
 
• Protruding furrowed tongue
 
• Chromosomal Aberrations
 
• Mild to moderate developmental disabilities
 
• Typical dermatoglyphic patterns (palm and fingerprint patterns)
 
 
 
 
 
• Recognizing the need to support people suffering from Down Syndrome, the WHO **on 20th December 2007, recognised March 21st as ‘World Down Syndrome Day’.**
